notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: 1500m INTERVAL Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 2000m at target 1500m Race Pace / Aerobic Power Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 8 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 150s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

coachingNotes: Build specific race pace rhythm over progressive mid-distance intervals.
Ensure active recovery jogs stay slow and conversational.
Focus on running tall, relaxed shoulders, and high back kick.
commonMistakes: Running recovery runs too fast, which interferes with physiological adaptation.
Straining on hills instead of backing off the effort.
safetyNotes: Stay fully hydrated and check heart rate responses on hot or humid training days.
Halt execution immediately if experiencing any sharp joint or muscular pain.
Choose a flat, well-lit surface with clean traction for speed work.

sourceNote: Workout design informed by research on energy system demands, training distribution, and recovery best practices.

trainingPurpose.practicalUse: Promotes blood flow and active tissue recovery without excessive musculoskeletal stress.
trainingPurpose.notFor: Avoid when suffering from acute systemic fatigue or high-grade tendon soreness.

executionCues: Keep the effort conversational; you should be able to speak in full sentences.
Focus on a relaxed posture, dropping your shoulders.
Maintain a soft, quick footstrike underneath your center of gravity.

startIf: No sharp pain in muscles or joints.
Breathing feels normal during the warmup jog.
Legs feel responsive during light stride checks.
modifyIf: Sleep was poor (under 6 hours) or hydration is low.
Muscles feel unusually stiff but no sharp pain.
Warmup feels sluggish.
skipIf: Sharp pain that causes limping or gait compensation.
Feeling dizzy, lightheaded, or having systemic symptoms.
Elevated resting heart rate indicating under-recovery.

environmentAdjustments.track: Use lanes consistently. Check direction rules to protect hips.
environmentAdjustments.road: Choose flat, traffic-free paths. Run on soft shoulders if available.
environmentAdjustments.treadmill: Use 1-2% incline to simulate wind resistance and match road effort.
environmentAdjustments.hotWeather: Reduce target speed by 5-10%. Extend recovery intervals as needed.
environmentAdjustments.hills: Maintain steady effort, not pace, when running uphill.

makeEasier: Reduce the total count of repetitions by 1-2.
Extend the recovery time by 30-60 seconds.
Run at a slightly more relaxed effort level.
makeHarder: Add 1-2 repetitions, maintaining the same target pace.
Slightly shorten recoveries or transition to an active float recovery.
Complete the final repeat slightly faster while maintaining form.
doNotProgressIf: Pace drops by more than 5% across intervals.
Form begins to break down or coordination is lost.
Persistent muscle tightness or sharp pain is felt.

riskReasons: Repetitive pounding over hard surfaces.
Neuromuscular fatigue might impact foot strike landing alignment.
riskProfile.saferAlternative: Move the workout to a track or soft grass surface to reduce joint impact forces.
